title: The Phantom of the Opera
tagline: Leave Box Five empty and the brulee unbroken.
about: In 1870s Paris, a young chorus girl at the opera house is coached in secret by a masked genius who lives in the tunnels beneath the stage.
cue: Serve the gougeres when the new managers are shown round the opera house in the middle of rehearsal.
faces: after dark, for dinner and a film at

    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersOpera managers' gougeresCrisp, hollow choux puffs baked with gruyere, dijon and black pepper, served warmHow to make it125ml milk100g butter1/2 tsp salt150g plain flour4 eggs150g gruyere, finely grated1 tsp dijon mustard1/2 tsp ground black pepperHeat the oven to 200°C. Bring the milk, 125ml water, butter and salt to the boil, tip in the flour and beat over the heat until it comes away from the pan.Cool 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time, then 120g of the gruyere, the mustard and pepper.Pipe or spoon walnut-sized balls onto lined trays and scatter with the rest of the gruyere.Bake until puffed and deep golden, and serve warm.Underground lake smoked trout rillettesHot-smoked trout folded with butter, crème fraîche, lemon, chives and capers, with toasted baguette and cornichonsHow to make it300g hot-smoked trout150g butter, softened100g crème fraîche1 lemon, zested and juiced1 bunch chives, finely chopped1 tbsp baby capers, chopped1/2 tsp ground white pepper1 baguette, sliced and toasted100g cornichonsFlake the trout, checking for bones.Mash with the butter, crème fraîche, lemon zest and juice, chives, capers and pepper, leaving it coarse.Pack into a dish, smooth the top and chill until set.Serve with the toasted baguette and cornichons.MainsThe new patron's steak frites with bearnaiseSeared sirloin with double-fried chips, watercress and a warm tarragon and shallot bearnaiseHow to make it4 sirloin steaks, about 250g each1 tbsp olive oil3 tbsp white wine vinegar1 shallot, finely chopped1 bunch tarragon, leaves chopped2 egg yolks180g butter, melted1kg large potatoes, cut into chips1.5 L vegetable oil, for frying2 tsp salt1 tsp cracked black pepper1 bunch watercressCut the potatoes into chips, rinse and dry, then fry at 140°C in batches until soft but pale.Simmer the vinegar, shallot, half the tarragon and 2 tbsp water down to 1 tbsp and strain.Whisk the reduction and egg yolks in a bowl over simmering water until thick, then whisk in the melted butter in a thin stream. Stir in the rest of the tarragon and keep warm.Rub the steaks with the oil, half the salt and the pepper and sear in a very hot pan 3 minutes a side, then rest 5 minutes.Fry the chips again at 190°C until crisp and golden, and toss with the rest of the salt.Serve the steaks with the chips, the bearnaise and watercress.Masquerade sole meunièreBrown butter, lemon and capers, for the masked ball supperHow to make it4 sole or flathead fillets, about 150g each50g plain flour100g butter1 tbsp olive oil2 lemons2 tbsp capers1 small bunch parsley800g baby potatoesBoil the potatoes in salted water until tender, drain and toss with a knob of the butter.Season the fish and dust in the flour, shaking off the extra.Fry the fish in the oil and a little butter until golden on both sides. Lift onto warm plates.Add the rest of the butter to the pan and cook until nutty brown, then add the capers, juice of a lemon and chopped parsley. Spoon over the fish.SweetsRed rose creme bruleeBaked vanilla and rosewater custard over crushed raspberries, chilled and topped with a crackling burnt sugar crustHow to make it500ml thickened cream1 vanilla bean, split6 egg yolks140g caster sugar1 tsp rosewater100g raspberries1 handful edible rose petals, optionalHeat the oven to 150°C and warm the cream with the vanilla until steaming.Whisk the yolks with 80g of the sugar, pour in the hot cream, stir in the rosewater and strain.Crush the raspberries into 4 ramekins, pour over the custard and bake in a water bath until just set.Cool, then chill.Scatter the rest of the sugar over the tops, burn with a blowtorch or under a very hot grill and top with rose petals.DrinksNew Year's Eve kir royaleBlackcurrant liqueur topped with chilled dry sparkling wine in a flute, with fresh blackberriesHow to make it80ml blackcurrant liqueur750ml dry sparkling wine12 blackberriesChill the sparkling wine and 4 flutes.Pour 20ml blackcurrant liqueur into each flute.Top slowly with sparkling wine and drop in a few blackberries.
